title: Imamun Nisha v. State of U.P.
coram: Siddhartha Varma, J.; Dr. Yogendra Kumar Srivastava, J.
disposition: Writ disposed of; Clause 6.5 representation to be decided in 10 days.
headnote: Writ against an electricity demand notice disposed of on the licensee's statement that the consumer's objection would be treated as a representation under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and decided within ten days, with no coercive action until then.
facts: The petitioner received a Demand Notice dated 1 September 2024 and approached the Electricity Department contending that the notice had been sent to her erroneously. She then filed this writ petition. Counsel for the Electricity Department stated that the objection already moved would be treated as an objection or representation under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, decided within ten days, and that no coercive action would be taken in the meantime.

holding_units.topic: billing objection treated as Clause 6.5 representation
holding_units.holding: An objection to a demand notice already moved before the Electricity Department is to be treated as a representation under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and decided within ten days; no coercive action is to be taken until the representation is decided or that period expires, whichever is earlier.

not_decided.point: Whether the Demand Notice dated 01.09.2024 was sent erroneously, and the merits of the demand
not_decided.note: Left to the Clause 6.5 authority to decide the representation within ten days.
